sections.content: How many people stayed in Yarm after gaining qualifications?

Yarm is a small town in the North East. Yarm does not have its own university.

Yarm has lower levels of deprivation.

Overall, Yarm ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • fewer non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 880 state-school pupils from Yarm who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 440 (50%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 280 (32%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Yarm to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Yarm's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Yarm in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Yarm move to?

Of Yarm's graduates, 230 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 65 of those graduates (28%) were living fairly locally, in the Middlesbrough and Stockton travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Yarm's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 105 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 65 of those qualified non-graduates (62%) were living fairly locally, in the Middlesbrough and Stockton travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Yarm's GCSE cohort:

  • 140 graduates left the North East
  • the most common region they moved to was Yorkshire and The Humber
  • 30 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the North East

In 2018 to 2019, 29% of graduates and 24% of qualified non-graduates living in Yarm had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 280 graduates and 225 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Yarm. This is compared with the 440 graduates and 280 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 71% of the graduates had also lived in Yarm as GCSE pupils, while 29% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Yarm in 2018 to 2019, 76% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 24% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
